# Previous-build checkpoint fixtures

`progression-v9-entities.bin`, `progression-v9-runtime.json` and
`server-v3-entities.json` were generated by the unmodified Termcraft library at
commit **ebc0447** (before extended item/fireball fields), using
`native-v9-generator.rs` as its example executable. The binary starts with native
version 9; the server JSON has version 3. All worlds and identifiers are disposable.

The fixture visits all three dimensions and includes multiple loose items and
fireballs, a wounded/aged villager, a wounded zombie, a wounded Nether blaze,
crystals and the dragon. Tests compare every dimension field against the old
writer's JSON, then save/reopen using the new format. This catches binary layout
breaks that same-version round-trip tests cannot detect.

To regenerate, export `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `src/` from `ebc0447` into a
fresh temporary checkout. Copy the generator to
`examples/native_v9_fixture.rs`. Build it with that checkout's manifest and a
separate `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. Run it against a fresh temporary save directory,
then run it again against that directory with `--export-server`. Copy only the
three fixture files into this directory. Never use a real player's save.

The separate interim-v9 test covers the brief development build `734efd8`, whose
new entity fields preceded the explicit format bump. Both old layouts retain
normal strict validation. Current writers use native v11 and server v5.

`progression-v10-entities.bin`, `progression-v10-runtime.json` and
`server-v4-entities.json` were written by the unmodified library at **a371169**,
using `native-v10-generator.rs` in a fresh `/tmp` export with its own Cargo target.
They include all creature families and old fields, worn thrown gear and reflected
fireballs across three dimensions. Tests compare the complete old runtime after
removing only newly defaulted hazard fields. This verifies the binary layout,
rather than constructing an alleged old save with the current writer.
